k: He ﷺ spent the nights of tashriq in Mina (Aishah, Abu Dawud {1}) and permitted only those with a duty elsewhere to miss them (Bukhari {2}).

"We used to wait till the sun declined, then do the rami" (Ibn Umar, Bukhari {1}); "on the days after (Nahr) he stoned after the zenith of the sun" (Tirmidhi {2}). He ﷺ stoned the first with seven pebbles saying takbir with each, went forward, faced the qibla and made a long dua; the same at the middle one; and did not stop after Aqabah (Bukhari {3}).
The days of tashriq are "days of eating, drinking and the remembrance of Allah" (Sahih Muslim); takbir after the prayers in these days is the practice of the companions.

"Whoever hastens in two days there is no sin on him, and whoever delays, there is no sin on him" (Quran {1}). The Prophet ﷺ himself stayed for the {2}th, remaining in Mina through the days of tashriq (Aishah, Abu Dawud {3}).
Exactly as the {1}th: after the sun declines, small→middle→Aqabah, takbir with every pebble, dua after the first two (Bukhari {2}, {3}; Tirmidhi {4}).
Having stayed, the night of the {1}th belongs to the nights of Mina, which the Prophet ﷺ spent there (Aishah, Abu Dawud {2}).
The third day of stoning, after the sun declines (Bukhari {1}; Tirmidhi {2}). Hanafis allow this last day's rami before midday.

The Prophet ﷺ bathed before ihram (Tirmidhi {1}) and was perfumed by Aishah (RA) before assuming it (Bukhari {2}). On the {3}th his companions who had done Umrah assumed ihram for Hajj from where they were staying in Makkah (Muslim {4}, {5}).
Anas (RA) was asked where the Prophet ﷺ prayed Dhuhr and Asr on the Day of Tarwiyah: "at Mina" (Bukhari {1}). He prayed two rakahs there (Bukhari {2}, {3}).
He ﷺ stayed in Mina until the sun rose on the {1}th, then moved to Arafah (Muslim {2}).

Ihram is the pillar that opens the Hajj — "actions are but by intentions" (Bukhari {1}). The companions did exactly this on the Day of Tarwiyah: "we assumed ihram for Hajj from al-Abtah" (Jabir, Muslim {2}).
Those who had a sacrificial animal with them did not leave ihram after the arrival tawaf and sa'i: "I cannot finish my ihram till I slaughter my hady" (Bukhari {1}).
The Prophet ﷺ "kept on reciting the talbiyah till he did the rami of Jamrat al-Aqabah" (Bukhari {1}).

"All of Arafah is a place of standing" (Muslim {1}, Abu Dawud {2}); the exclusion of the hollow of Uranah comes from Ibn Majah {3} (weak chain) and the Muwatta, and the schools agree on it. The Prophet ﷺ camped at Namirah until the sun declined, then moved into Arafah (Muslim {4}).
"The best of supplication is the supplication of the Day of Arafah, and the best of what I and the prophets before me have said is: la ilaha illallah…" (Tirmidhi {1}).
"When you pour down from Arafat, remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram" (Quran {1}). He ﷺ "made takbir, tahlil and dua" there (Muslim {2}).

On the morning of Aqabah the Prophet ﷺ asked Ibn Abbas (RA) to pick up pebbles for him — small ones, "pebbles for flicking" (hasa al-khadhf, about the size of a chickpea or a date stone) — and said "like these; beware of going to extremes" (Nasai {1}, Ibn Majah {2}).
He ﷺ "offered Maghrib and Isha together at al-Muzdalifah" (Bukhari {1}), with one adhan and two iqamahs and no sunnah prayers between them (Muslim {2}; Bukhari {3}).

He ﷺ lay down until dawn, prayed Fajr early, then stood at al-Mash'ar al-Haram making takbir, tahlil and dua "until the sky became very bright", and left before sunrise (Muslim {1}). Allah says: "remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram" (Quran {2}).

The Prophet ﷺ sent the weak of his family ahead on the night of Muzdalifah (Bukhari {1}); Ibn Umar (RA) would send them ahead by night (Bukhari {2}); Asma (RA) left when the moon set and stoned the Jamrah before Fajr (Bukhari {3}).

He ﷺ prayed Dhuhr and Asr together at Dhuhr time with one adhan and two iqamahs (Jabir, Muslim {1}), shortened to two rakahs each. Salim told al-Hajjaj, and Ibn Umar (RA) confirmed it: "if you want to follow the sunnah, pray early, just after midday, on the Day of Arafah" (Bukhari {2}).
He ﷺ stayed "until the sun had set" and then departed (Muslim {1}), moving calmly, holding his camel back, telling the people: "calmness, calmness" (Muslim {2}).

"Hajj is Arafah. Whoever comes [to Arafah] on the night of Jam' (the night before the {1}th), before Fajr, has caught the Hajj" (Tirmidhi {2}). He ﷺ stood facing the qibla, hands raised, until the sun set (Nasai {3}, Muslim {4}).

The Prophet ﷺ ordered it as the last act before leaving (Bukhari {1}, Muslim). He ﷺ himself did it at night, after Isha and a short sleep at al-Muhassab, before setting out for Madinah (Anas, Bukhari {2}).
"No one should depart until the last thing he does is the House" (Ibn Majah {1}) — so the shopping, the packing and the goodbyes come first.
The same command — "except the menstruating women, who were excused" (Bukhari {1}). When Safiyyah (RA) got her period after tawaf al-ifadah, the Prophet ﷺ said: "then depart" (Bukhari {2}).
The companions bared their right shoulders to show Quraysh their strength; the Prophet ﷺ kept the practice in the arrival tawaf.
The jog between the lights marks the dip in the valley where Hajar ran "like a person in distress" (Bukhari {1}).
"Take the Maqam of Ibrahim as a place of prayer" (Quran {1}) — the Prophet ﷺ recited this very verse then prayed there (Muslim {2}).
He repeated the same praise and dua on each hill (Muslim {1}) — persistence in dua is the lesson of sa'i.
"Actions are but by intentions" (Bukhari {1}). The miqats are boundaries the Prophet ﷺ himself appointed (Bukhari {2}).
Seven is the number the Prophet ﷺ performed; keeping count is itself part of the reward (Tirmidhi {1}).
"I begin with what Allah began with" (Muslim {1}) — Safa is named first in Quran {2}.
The Prophet ﷺ entered ihram at Dhul-Hulayfah after praying there — beginning the journey with salah is his way.
'Umar (RA) kissed the Stone saying "I know you are a stone… had I not seen the Prophet ﷺ kiss you I would not" (Bukhari {1}) — pure following, not superstition.
The talbiyah is your answer to Ibrahim's call (Quran {1}); the Prophet's ﷺ own words are recorded in Bukhari {2}.
"Tawaf around the House is like salah" (Tirmidhi {1}) — so it needs the purity of salah.
He touched the Yamani corner (Bukhari {1}) — no sound report has him kissing it — and recited this dua between the two corners (Abu Dawud {2}).
After the two rakahs he ﷺ drank Zamzam and poured some on his head before sa'i (Musnad Ahmad {1}, from Jabir) — you follow his sequence step for step.

{1}–{2} Dhul Hijjah — the {3}th if you stay — then the farewell. Tap a day to open it in the rites guide.

Cannot afford a hady? The Quran's own alternative: fast three days during Hajj and seven days when you are home. Best the {1}th–{2}th (Shafi'i) or the {3}th–{4}th (Hanafi / Hanbali — the {5}th is allowed for the one who owes this fast). Missed them? Malikis and Hanbalis allow the days of tashriq (Bukhari {6}–{7}), as does al-Shafi'i's old view; the relied-upon Shafi'i view does not, so the three days are made up later; Hanafis say the hady is then owed instead. Forgot to arrange it? It may be slaughtered until sunset on the {8}th according to Hanafis, Malikis and Hanbalis, or the {9}th according to many contemporary scholars (Shafi'is set no last day, though the {10}th is best); after that most scholars say it is still owed and must be made up. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

Changed into normal clothes before cutting? Put the ihram back on if you can and cut now. Whether a fidyah is owed differs: Shafi'is and Hanbalis excuse clothing worn forgetfully or unknowingly, but not cutting hair or nails; Hanafis require it regardless, and so do Malikis unless you had already stoned (for them the stoning alone opens the first tahallul); some Hanbalis and many contemporary scholars say nothing is owed for forgetting or not knowing (Bukhari {1}) — a fast of {2} days, feeding {3} poor, or a sheep (Quran {4}; the amounts are from Bukhari {5}). Shaved before the hady or before the rami? "No harm" (Bukhari {6}) for Shafi'is and Hanbalis; Hanafis: a dam; Malikis: a fidyah for shaving before the rami. Left Makkah without ever cutting? Cut as soon as you remember, wherever you are — until then intimacy stays forbidden. Hanafis and Malikis say a dam is owed; Shafi'is and Hanbalis say nothing is owed for the delay. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.
Did an errand afterwards and the bus has not left? Simply do the tawaf again. Already left? See the next step, and tell your group leader / ask a scholar.
